## Objective
Replace the contract stub `src/game.js` with the real implementation of the pure, DOM-free Snake rules. The module is the single source of truth for game state; the browser layer built in T3 only calls these functions and draws the result. This task exists so the logic can be verified entirely with `node --test` and no browser.

## Interface
`src/game.js` is an ES module. Keep every export of the existing stub with the same names and signatures (the file at that path is replaced, not extended):
```js
export const DEFAULT_WIDTH = 20;
export const DEFAULT_HEIGHT = 20;
export const INITIAL_LENGTH = 3;
export const DIRECTIONS; // { up:{x:0,y:-1}, down:{x:0,y:1}, left:{x:-1,y:0}, right:{x:1,y:0} }
export function createGame(options?: { width?: number, height?: number, rng?: () => number }): GameState;
export function placeFood(width: number, height: number, snake: Point[], rng: () => number): Point | null;
export function setDirection(state: GameState, direction: Direction): GameState;
export function step(state: GameState, rng?: () => number): GameState;
export function tickInterval(score: number): number;
```
Types (`GameState`, `Point`, `Direction`, `Status`) are the JSDoc typedefs already in the stub; keep them. `rng` defaults to `Math.random`.

## Behavior
1. `createGame` validates `width` and `height` (defaults `DEFAULT_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_HEIGHT`): each must be an integer of at least 5, otherwise throw `RangeError`.
2. `createGame` builds a snake of `INITIAL_LENGTH` cells in a horizontal line, head at `{x: Math.floor(width/2), y: Math.floor(height/2)}` and the body extending to the left (`x-1`, `x-2`). `direction` and `nextDirection` are `'right'`, `score` is 0, `status` is `'running'`, and `food` comes from `placeFood` with the supplied `rng`.
3. `placeFood` lists every cell not occupied by the snake in row order (y outer loop, x inner loop), returns the cell at index `Math.floor(rng() * freeCount)` clamped to `freeCount - 1`, and returns `null` when there are no free cells.
4. `setDirection` returns the same state object when `state.status` is not `'running'`, when `direction` is not one of the four names in `DIRECTIONS`, or when `direction` is the opposite of `state.direction` (not of `nextDirection`). Otherwise it returns a new state with `nextDirection` set.
5. `step` returns the same state object when `status` is not `'running'`.
6. Otherwise `step` sets `direction` to `nextDirection` and computes the new head by adding the `DIRECTIONS` delta to `snake[0]`.
7. If the new head is outside `0 <= x < width` and `0 <= y < height`, return a copy of the state with the updated `direction`, the snake unchanged, and `status: 'over'`.
8. If the new head equals a body cell the result is `status: 'over'` with the snake unchanged. When no food is eaten this move, the current tail cell does not count as a body cell because it moves away. When food is eaten, every existing cell counts.
9. Eating means the new head equals `state.food`. The new snake is the new head followed by all old cells (the tail is kept, length grows by one), `score` increases by 1, and `food` becomes `placeFood(width, height, newSnake, rng)`. If that is `null` the status becomes `'won'`.
10. Without eating, the new snake is the new head followed by all old cells except the last.
11. `step` never mutates its input: it returns fresh `snake` arrays and fresh point objects.
12. `tickInterval(score)` returns `Math.max(70, 150 - 5 * score)`.

## Invariants
- No DOM access, no `window`, no timers, no randomness other than through the `rng` parameter (default `Math.random`).
- The module has no imports and no side effects at load.
- Exports keep the same names so `src/main.js` (T3) can import them.

## Edge cases
- Eating the last free cell: the snake fills the board, `placeFood` returns `null`, status `'won'`, `food` `null`.
- `rng` returning exactly 1 (out of contract) must not index past the end; clamp the index.
- A hand-made state may use a board size other than 20 by 20; always read `state.width` and `state.height`.
- A snake of length 2 or 3 never self-collides on a straight move; collision logic must still not throw on short snakes.

## Guardrails
- Do not modify anything under `test/`; those files are protected and graded.
- Do not touch `src/controls.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html` or `package.json`.
- Do not add dependencies or a build step.

## Out of scope
Keyboard handling, drawing, timers, the speed-up loop, high scores, and any DOM work (all in T3 or nowhere).
